brief: The canvas displays a perpetually active sheet of distressed, vintage paper upon which text appears continuously, character by character. This text stream is generated automatically, mimicking the rhythm of a typewriter gaining speed and confidence. As the text accumulates, the physical surface of the paper reacts to the stress, visually transitioning through several phases of decay: first, a subtle warping; next, deep, permanent creases form along the print path; subsequent stresses lead to noticeable hairline fractures webbing the surface; and finally, the constant action causes the paper fibers to visibly fray and pull away from the printed characters, creating a dynamic, deteriorating surface.

statement: This sketch depicts a vintage paper sheet that gradually deteriorates as text scrolls across it in a typewriter rhythm. The paper begins with subtle warping effects and evolves through permanent creases, hairline fractures, and finally fiber fraying—each stage visualized through layered visual elements that respond to the accumulating text. The viewer observes a continuous, self-contained process of decay that mirrors the physical stress of writing on aged paper, all without any external interaction required.
